blocks.text: Sara joined the school newspaper as a photographer and seldom offered opinions in meetings. While the writers rushed to finish stories, she kept a small table of every number the paper printed. Before the issue about the canteen survey went out, she noticed something odd: the article said 70 percent of students liked the new menu, but only 120 of the 300 forms said so. The editor checked the forms and found that the writer had counted the same pile twice. The story was corrected just in time. At the end of the term, the editor gave Sara a new role. "Checking facts," he explained, "is as important as telling stories."
1. What was wrong with the canteen article?
A. It used an old photo.    B. Its percentage did not match the forms.    C. It was printed too late.    D. It criticised the cooks.
2. What can we infer about Sara?
A. She was careful with details.    B. She wanted to be a writer.    C. She disliked the new menu.    D. She often argued with the editor.
3. What new role was Sara most probably given?
A. Photographer.    B. Fact checker.    C. Canteen manager.    D. Story writer.

design.method: 定位证据句→推断人物特点→理解结尾观点
